    AI Overview
    E15 is
    a fuel blend containing 15% ethanol and 85% gasoline, commonly sold as Unleaded 88. Approved for 2001 and newer vehicles, it is popular for being cheaper, higher in octane (88 vs. 87), and burning cleaner than E10. It is often used to lower pump prices but is not recommended for older vehicles, motorcycles, or small engines. 
    Key Aspects of E15 Fuel: 
    • Availability & Cost: E15 is available at over 3,000 stations, particularly in the Midwest, and often costs 10–30 cents less per gallon than regular gas.
    • Vehicle Compatibility: Safe for about 96% of vehicles on the road, including cars, light-duty trucks, and SUVs from model year 2001 or newer.
    • Performance & Emissions: It has a higher octane rating (88 vs 87), providing better engine performance, and reduces greenhouse gas emissions by roughly 40-50% compared to conventional gasoline.
    • Restrictions: It should not be used in motorcycles, boats, and small engines like lawnmowers or chainsaws.
    • Regulatory Status: The EPA has issued emergency waivers for continued summer sales (beyond May 1) to reduce fuel prices, despite concerns over increased evaporation in warm weather. 
    e15 Design (Alternative Result)
    The e15 brand is also a luxury furniture company based in Germany, recognized for its modern designs like the ALDE seating collection. 
    For the purpose of fuel, E15 is a widely approved, cost-effective, and cleaner-burning alternative to standard E10 fuel, largely available in the US.
